entries.final_answer: Two write paths still race charter synthesis without the run-wide synthesis lock (#6453). (1) charter activate/deactivate write the activation config outside the lock, so a deactivation that lands inside a synthesis run's activation-append window is lost: synthesis's stale read either overwrites it or the deactivation refuses with precondition_changed and the artifact stays in force. (2) The activation-ledger migration's manifest stamp (activation_ledger._stamp_manifest) reads and rewrites the whole synthesis manifest unlocked, so it can drop manifest entries a concurrent synthesis run just wrote. Grounded on main at 6f73b2a98e: neither writer takes the lock (issue #6719).
entries.question: What problem does this Mission solve?

entries.final_answer: A two-writer test proves each race is closed: (a) a charter deactivate that races a synthesis activation append stays deactivated and the append survives, instead of one writer failing with precondition_changed or dropping the other's write; (b) apply_ledger_migration's manifest stamp cannot drop synthesis manifest entries written concurrently. Both writers hold the existing run-wide synthesis lock for their whole read-modify-write, a held lock is a bounded wait then a coded CHARTER_SYNTHESIS_LOCK_HELD refusal with nothing written, and the existing synthesis-lock, activation and migration suites stay green (issue #6719).
entries.question: How will we know this Mission is successful?

entries.final_answer: Out of scope: inventing a new lock or lock scope (the existing run-wide synthesis lock from #6453 is reused); the compiled-catalog write reached from the post-write recompile_or_notify (a staleness question re-derived by the next synthesis run, not a lost-write one); activation writers other than activate/deactivate/preset/the org-required promotion primitive and the ledger migration; and any change to the other pre-existing red-on-main suites (#6798, #6801, #6816, #5927).
